source_title: Punjab, Odisha and Tamil Nadu in race to host 2030 FIH Hockey World Cups - Sportstar
source_excerpt:
FILE PHOTO: Men’s World Cup defender Germany during the 2026 podium ceremony in Wavre, Belgium. | Photo Credit: AP
Punjab, Odisha and Tamil Nadu are the frontrunners to host the 2030 FIH World Cups for both men and women, Hockey India secretary general Bhola Nath Singh confirmed to PTI .
This development confirms that India is eyeing the hosting rights for the next edition of the showpiece events.
Odisha has hosted the men’s World Cup twice, while Tamil Nadu organised the men’s Junior World Cup last year in Chennai and Madurai.
Punjab, regarded as the cradle of Indian hockey, has never hosted the mega event. The state is currently hosting the men’s Asian Champions Trophy, its first international hockey tournament in 17 years. The last international hockey event hosted by Punjab was the Gold Cup in 2009.
“Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Punjab are all in the race. If Odisha gets the Hockey World Cup, it will be a big achievement for the state. Odisha will be the first preference,” Bhola Nath said.

The HI secretary general said his primary focus since taking charge had been to take hockey to every corner of the country.
“I want to take hockey to every corner of the country. Tamil Nadu has produced many Olympians, and we took the Junior World Cup there last year. Punjab is now an example. We are now taking the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy to Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh. No international tournament has been held in Madhya Pradesh so far. The women’s ACT will be held from November 19 to 28 in Bhopal,” he said.
“The purpose of taking hockey to every part of the country is to build infrastructure of international standards.”
Bhola Nath said Punjab was chosen to host the ongoing Asian Champions Trophy because of its rich hockey legacy and the significant number of players from the state in the national squad.
“When I became the secretary general of Hockey India, I saw that most of the players in the team were from Punjab. When I spoke to the boys from Punjab, they used to say that they had played in countries across the world, but their parents had never seen them play an international match. So, I wanted to organise an international tournament in Punjab,” he said.
“The talks were going on, and one day I met Bhagwant Mann (Punjab Chief Minister) and discussed this with him. He said he was ready and would do it.”
